spans.s: ubhayaṃ, in cobhayaṃ (= Pali cūbhayaṃ, PTSD s.v. ubhaya), both, after two coordinates: krīḍanti ramanti cobhayaṃ MPS 〔12.9〕, they sport and take delight both.

ubhayato-bhāga-vimukta, adj. (= Pali ubhatobhāga-vimutta), emancipated from both parts: Mvy 〔1028〕 (misprinted ˚bhaga˚; corr. Index); Divy 〔404.24〕 (read: ubhau hi tau ubhayatobhāgavimuktau); Bhīk 〔27b.1〕; cf. AbhidhK. LaV-P. 〔ii.205〕; 〔vi.275—7〕. Often edd. (Pali and BHS) print ubha(ya)to as separate word, wrongly; it modifies bhāga- directly, as part of the cpd. Tib. on Mvy gñis kaḥi cha las … from both parts; Pali MN comm. 〔iii.188.7〕 = DN comm. 〔ii.514.3〕 dvīhi bhāgehi vimutto, arūpasamāpattiyā rūpakāyato vimutto, maggena nāmakāyato (i.e. from the skhandha other than rūpa) vimutto. The AbhidhK. 〔vi.276〕 has a different interpretation acc. to LaV-P., delivered from the obstacle of the passions (impurities, kleśāvaraṇa), and from the obstacle to (the 8) vimokṣa (which is stated to be akarmaṇyatā, lʼimpuissance corporelle [] et mentale). This seems to be a later reinterpretation; the Pali comms. make it simpler, referring to the physical and mental constituents. Which was meant in our texts is not clear from the contexts.
ubhayavyañjana, adj., f. ˚nā (= Pali ubhatobyañjanaka), having the marks of both (sexes), hermaphrodite: ˚naḥ Mvy 〔8775〕; ˚nā Bhīk 〔11a.4〕; 〔16a.5〕 (in questioning a candidate for ordination).
